n: While revising the Bible, Joseph Smith asked questions about the book of Revelation. The first: the “sea of glass” John saw before God’s throne is the earth in its future sanctified, immortal, eternal state.

The four beasts are symbolic figures describing heaven and the happiness of all God’s creatures—people, animals, birds. Spiritual things resemble physical ones and vice versa; even animals have spirits in the likeness of their bodies.

f.w: that which is spiritual being in the likeness of that which is temporal

n: The four beasts John saw were individual beings, but they represent the glory of whole classes of creatures in their eternal sphere and happiness.
The beasts’ eyes symbolize light and knowledge; their wings symbolize power to move and act.
The twenty-four elders were faithful ministers who had died, belonged to the seven churches of Asia, and were in God’s paradise.
The book sealed with seven seals contains God’s will, mysteries, and works concerning the earth during its seven-thousand-year temporal existence—understood as the period since the Fall.

f.w: sealed on the back with seven seals

n: Each seal represents a thousand years: the first seal the first thousand years, and so on to the seventh.

The four angels of Revelation 7 are sent from God with power over the earth’s four quarters to save or destroy. They carry the everlasting gospel to every nation, with power to seal to life or cast down.

The angel ascending from the east holds the seal of the living God over Israel’s twelve tribes and tells the four angels to wait until God’s servants are sealed. He is identified as an “Elias” who gathers Israel and restores all things.

f.w: the angel ascending from the east

f.g: A title for a forerunner or restorer, applied to several messengers.

n: These events take place in the sixth thousand-year period, at the opening of the sixth seal.
The 144,000 sealed from Israel’s tribes are high priests ordained to administer the gospel, called from every nation to bring all who will come into the Church of the Firstborn.

f.w: the one hundred and forty-four thousand

n: As God created the world in six days and sanctified the seventh, so at the start of the seventh thousand years he will sanctify the earth, complete salvation, and judge. The seven trumpets prepare the way for Christ’s coming.

f.w: on the seventh day he finished his work

n: The events of Revelation 9 occur after the seventh seal opens but before Christ comes. So the Second Coming follows a period of trouble within the seventh thousand years.
The little book John ate represents a mission and ordinance for him to gather Israel. John is an Elias, a restorer of all things.

f.w: the little book which was eaten by John

n: The two witnesses are two prophets raised up for the Jewish people in the last days, prophesying in Jerusalem after the Jews are gathered and the city is rebuilt.
